forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Milton Keynes used all its remaining schools surplus to balance 2026/27, and expects a high needs deficit
news_drafts.lead:
Milton Keynes City Council used all of its remaining brought-forward surplus on special educational needs funding to balance the 2026/27 budget, and expects to start 2027/28 in deficit on that spending, papers for the Budget and Resources Scrutiny Committee on 6 October show. The money is in the "high needs" block, the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities, paid for from the dedicated schools grant (the government grant that funds schools).

The council's medium-term financial outlook says costs on high needs are running ahead of government funding. It says "there is a chance that the block will go into a deficit during the 2026/27 if there were to be any in year overspend", so "it is therefore likely we may start the 2027/28 financial year in a deficit." A separate General Fund annex, covering the council's main day-to-day budget, says the block "is expected to go into Deficit in 2026/27". It says the effect on that budget is unclear "as we await Government announcements on whether there will be any financial support." The paper gives no figure for the deficit. A review with the high needs school reference group is under way to find savings.

A statutory override, a temporary government rule that keeps such deficits off a council's main balance sheet, lets them be carried forward until 2028. The paper estimates councils with schools responsibilities hold about £5 billion of high needs deficits between them by the end of 2025/26. The council also says it will not receive its indicative 2027/28 schools funding until December 2026. Draft allocations "used to be published in July", it says, and this is the third year of delay. The full budget update will wait until then.

news_drafts.headline: Milton Keynes fills audit vacancies after control concerns emerge
news_drafts.lead: Milton Keynes Council has filled three vacancies in its internal audit team following concerns raised in September about stretched resources affecting the quality of financial oversight. The Audit Committee's annual report for 2025-26 shows that during the year, internal audit issued two reports with limited assurance opinions — meaning auditors identified significant control issues presenting high risk to how the council manages its finances and decision-making. The council has now put in place a framework for specialist audits as part of its efforts to address the resource shortfall that prevented internal audit from fully delivering its planned work.

news_drafts.headline: Milton Keynes has 82 outstanding audit recommendations including 23 new issues; council implemented 44 recommendations
news_drafts.lead: Milton Keynes council's internal audit committee heard that the pace of identifying problems is outstripping the council's ability to fix them. Of 82 audit recommendations outstanding as of August, 23 are new issues with implementation dates still in the future — nearly four times the six new recommendations identified a year ago. During the same period, the council successfully implemented 44 recommendations, but internal auditors found fresh control failures in schools, housing and children's services. A maintained school lost £12,000 to bank mandate fraud before detection, while the council's landlord rent-guarantee scheme lacks basic safeguards including a process to recover deposits. The audit committee's progress report shows auditors completed 29 audits in the year; four received limited assurance opinions, indicating design flaws in those areas' control systems.

findings.headline: Quarter 1 2026/27 General Fund underspend of £4.832m forecast, of which £1.3m is one-off and approximately £3.5m is ongoing
findings.detail: The Quarter 1 2026/27 Budget Monitoring Report forecasts a General Fund underspend of £4.832m against the 2026/27 approved budget. Of this, £1.3m relates to one-off items, meaning the ongoing position shows an underspend of approximately £3.5m. The council states it has reflected the ongoing impact of this favourable position within the MTFO where appropriate, suggesting it has been cautious about assuming in-year savings are available to support the medium-term outlook.
findings.matters: Shows whether budget assumptions are realistic and whether the council is generating in-year savings that can support forward planning; indicates budget setting may be prudent but also questions whether forecast is still valid
findings.figures: £4.832m total underspend Quarter 1 2026/27; £1.3m one-off items; approximately £3.5m ongoing
findings.quote: The Quarter 1 2026/27 Budget Monitoring Report currently forecasts a General Fund underspend of (£4.832m), of which £1.3m relates to one-off items.

findings.headline: High Needs Block (dedicated schools grant) expected to go into deficit in 2026/27; impact on General Fund unclear pending government announcements
findings.detail: The council expects the High Needs Block (funding for special educational provision) to move into deficit in 2026/27. The impact on the General Fund is currently unquantified and depends on government policy. The council is awaiting announcements on whether there will be any financial support or whether councils will be required to absorb such deficits from their main budgets. This represents a known but unquantified financial risk to the General Fund in 2026/27 and potentially beyond.
findings.matters: A known emerging deficit in the education budget that could require General Fund support; outcome depends on government announcements, creating uncertainty for medium-term planning
findings.figures: High Needs Block expected into deficit 2026/27; impact on General Fund currently unquantified
findings.quote: High Needs Block - is expected to go into Deficit in 2026/27 - Impact on GF Budget is currently unclear as we await Government announcements on whether there will be any financial support.

findings.headline: Savings programme expanded to £12.572m over four years (increase of £9.679m from February) but £3.840m further savings still unidentified
findings.detail: Milton Keynes has identified £9.679m of additional savings since February 2026, bringing total planned savings to £12.572m over the four-year period. The main vehicle is the 'Changing Because We Have To' (CBWHT) programme focused on productivity improvements and ensuring work is undertaken in-house only where appropriate. However, the updated forecast shows that even with these savings identified, a further £3.840m in savings must be found by 31 March 2031. Directors are currently developing detailed business cases for these additional measures.
findings.matters: Shows significant savings programme delivery but also that material unidentified savings are still required; raises questions about remaining deliverability and how the final gap will be closed
findings.figures: £12.572m total savings 2027/28-2030/31; £9.679m increase since February 2026; £3.840m further savings needed by 31/3/2031
findings.quote: The MTFO currently includes savings totalling £12.572m between 2027/28 and 2030/31. Based on the updated financial projection further savings of £3.840m are needed by 31/3/2031.

findings.headline: Utility cost inflation forecast at 15.1% for 2027/28, versus 5% annual increase assumed in February 2026
findings.detail: The February 2026 MTFP assumed utility costs would rise 5% annually from 2027/28 onwards. Updated forecasts from treasury advisors now indicate 15.1% inflation for 2027/28, before returning to 5% in subsequent years. This adds £0.317m to the 2027/28 base budget and reflects current energy market conditions. The large variance from assumption suggests exposure to external cost pressures and raises questions about other inflation forecasts used in the plan.
findings.matters: Reveals how external market factors can significantly shift budget assumptions mid-planning cycle; suggests inflation forecasts carry material downside risk and other assumptions may also miss
findings.figures: 15.1% utility inflation assumed 2027/28 vs 5% in February forecast; adds £0.317m to 2027/28
findings.quote: The February 2026 MTFP assumed a 5% annual increase in gas and electricity prices from 2027/28 onwards. Updated forecasts now indicate a 15.1% increase in 2027/28

findings.headline: Milton Keynes Waste Recovery Park contract with new operator from October 2026 adds £2.4m annual base budget pressure from 2027/28
findings.detail: The procurement for the waste recovery park has concluded with a new contractor commencing October 2026. Following tender conclusion, projected operational costs now exceed the previous £1.9m allowance by £0.5m, resulting in a £2.4m annual base budget pressure from 2027/28 onwards. The council notes actual net costs will depend on tonnages, recyclate prices, energy market prices, and plant running costs, creating exposure to external market factors and operator performance.
findings.matters: A new fixed annual cost commitment that persists through the planning period, with performance and market exposure; shows how major infrastructure contracts create structural budget dependencies
findings.figures: £2.4m annual pressure from 2027/28; £0.5m higher than previously estimated; contract commences October 2026
findings.quote: Following the conclusion of the tender and extension of the current contractor we now expect costs to be about £0.500m higher than previously projected and we have included this £2.400m as a base budget pressure from 2027/28.
